newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian companies law by next April - Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: Indian companies law by next April - Chidambaram.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Monday that he hopes a new law governing companies which would allow firms to issue derivatives and buy back shares to be in force by next April 1.

Chidambaram told a seminar organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) that he hoped to introduce a bill amending the Companies Act of 1956 during the monsoon sesssion of parliament, either in July or August.
He said he hoped parliament would adopt the law later in the year so it would take effect by April 1, 1998.
In February, a working group issued a report recommending sweeping changes in the companies law.
The report was the basis for a "working draft bill" which is open to changes and will later form the foundation for the bill to be presented to parliament, Chidambaram said.

The draft bill allows companies to buy back shares and issue hybrids, derivatives, options and quasi-equity instruments with differential rights. It also stiffens the punishment for violations of the Companies Act.
Chidambaram said the bill was still subject to public debate but would eventually have to embody certain principles.

He cited the greater degree of accountability which lies with public listed companies, the need to encourage corporate democracy, companies' responsibility to meet compliance and disclosure requirements and the need for corporate self-governance.

The CII released a background paper urging the government to drop a provision which would limit certain managers' remuneration, adjust a section on the computation of profits and abolish a measure requiring directors to retire at age 65.
